text_fidelity_a:
Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I'm a software developer who works in a cubicle world with the heating system droning on above the ceiling (we're on the top floor of an office building - the HVAC is on the roof). These headphones provide an oasis of silence! The noise cancellation *seems* to be a cut above the others I've tried (Beats Studio at Target and a Sony set at Costco) although it's not really fair to compare as I didn't try the Bose under the same condition as the others (i.e. in a noisy store).

How good is it? The droning AC noise is completely gone. Voices I can still hear - until I play music. Even at low/moderate playback volume, voices are barely audible. People have to pat me on the back if they want my attention.

Comfort is excellent. I wear them on-and-off all day without problems. I imagine people with big ears might be less comfortable.

Power: the headphones use a single AAA battery. Keeping in mind that I maybe play music for 2-3 hours every day, the battery seems to last 2-3 weeks. As others have noted, these headphones will not work (i.e. play music) without power.

My one nitpick (and the reason I can't give it 5 stars) is the god-awful chord. It's some cheap plasticky material that I continually have to unravel by dangling the headphones by the plug end and letting the headphones rotate. It's really quite pathetic to put such cheap cr$p on $300 headphones - shame on Bose for not correcting this. Is it really going to affect your profitability so much you can't do something like the $20 Apple headphones that come with every iPhone (they're more rubberized and don't seem to get raveled).

Update for iPhone/iPad/iPod users: with iOS 7, Apple introduced a new way to invoke Siri (Apple's voice assistant) - instead of holding down the home button (or center button on the headphones) until you hear the Siri confirmation sound and then asking Siri your question and then waiting for Siri to accept your input, with iOS 7, you can keep the button pressed until you're finished talking - and avoid the delay Siri normally waits to know you're done with talking. It's a very useful feature.....and, it doesn't work with the Bose inline chord button :-( Not really Bose's fault, I guess, but I thought it worth mentioning.
text_fidelity_b: Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
SquareTrade 4-year Office Protection Plan Purchased this 4 year plan in November 2016 on a Dell Laser Printer. Thus the printer was a little over 2 years when it started doing weird things and I made a claim.

Basically ... the printer stopped printing black ... it just got lighter and lighter. I attempted to clean the heads and change the cartridges to no avail. The printer would also keep running and not stop after done doing a printer job.

I printed my receipt / invoice off Amazon to PDF. I then went to SquareTrade's website attached the receipt. I then made a claim. The claim process was pretty easy and they actually approved me for a full refund. I just needed to fill out an affidavit. I did this but a week later I still had no refund. Somehow my affidavit didn't get logged even though I got a confirmation email. I called them on the telephone and they fixed everything and were kind about it. Within 24 hours they emailed me an Amazon gift certificate (my choice) which gave me an additional 5% back. I this received a $121 refund on an $118 printer that died in its 3rd year.

I have no complaints and would purchase a square trade warranty again.

Bits of interest as I read other people's low reviews:

1) You purchase a 4 year warranty, but really, for example, it is just 3 extra years beyond the purchase's original 1 year warranty (or however long applies). If your item dies in a year, you have to go to the manufacturer for help.

2) You need to have your receipt. No biggie. Amazon is super amazing that way. I can see all my order back to when Amazon just sold books. Print the invoice / receipt to PDF and there you go. Receipt. Proof of purchase.

3) There is no paper copy of this plan. This is great. It saves trees. You would probably lose it anyway. But Amazon also kept a copy of the fact that I purchased this along with the printer. It was in my order history. There is your proof and all the telephone numbers are there. It is so easy. You don't need a stack of papers.

4) If you file a claim and get 100% of your purchase price back, you cannot file a claim for the same item again. No brainer.

5) This isn't accident insurance. If you do a dumb thing like leave your camera on top of your husband's big rig fender and it ends up in a million pieces 1/2 mile from your house ... it is NOT covered. If you think it should be ... well then ... Take out an insurance policy ... not a warranty. Those are two different things.

6) If you got a deal and paid $65 for your item, but the item now sells for $400 ... you still only paid $65 and $65 is all you are getting back. You don't make money off warranties.
text_fidelity_b: SquareTrade 4-year Office Protection Plan

Belkin N150 Wireless USB Adapter with up to 150Mbps Link Rate I originally requested this product to review as the wireless card my newer laptop had broken and the wi-fi usb adapter I had didn't seem very fast. Then that laptop got completely broken. I am now using my older laptop that has a wireless card that works. So I thought I would try this anyway and see what happened.
The adapter comes with a CD for set up. You must have a CD_ROM drive to use this. It is very easy just click a few things and it installs in just a few minutes. And this really does make a difference. My internet is so much faster with this. There are a couple a websites I use that can take longer to load. But with this Belkin adapter, everything is much faster. I don't do any gaming but I do stream a lot of videos. They load faster now.
The only thing I don't like is that the adapter is about 2" long and 1" wide. It is much larger than the other adapter I have but that is probably why it works so much faster.
My wi-fi signal is stronger than it used to be in areas furthest from my router.
My router is Belkin as well. The box states this will work with all router brands but specifically lists these: Belkin, Netgear, Apple, D-Link, TENDnet, and TP-Link.
This seems like a good deal for the price, I really am loving the speed!

FYI: after awhile the blue blinking light from the adapter can me annoying, it is kind of bright. You might want to cover that with some dark tape.

update 8/29/14- this hasn't been working as well in the past few days, there stopped being a difference when I add it to my laptop. I'm disappointed.

Wall Outlet Extender Surge Protector - 6 Outlet Wall Adapter with 3 USB Charging Ports (1 USB-C, 2 USB A), Multi Plug Outlets Wall Mount with Top Phone Holder for Home, Dorm Essentail, 490 Joules There has been an unpleasant shift, from who is responsible for supplying the power adapters for USB powered appliances. And, for the number of simple household appliances that now require those adapters. I suppose that I can see the logic in it. Newer electrical devices now require lower power. Thence, adapters. At first, they came with the device, like cell phones were supplied with the wall adapters. Eventually, you had to buy your own adapters. Even now, you have to be careful in selecting an adapter. There are basic ones that only have 3 amps. Some have 5 amps or more. Some only split all their power between multiple ports. Some are 'smart' and provide all the amps needed to multiple devices. Now, that's pretty much the rule. You gotta do it yourself and you better know what you're looking for. Disappointment is more common than satisfaction, in this new game.

These outlet adapters from Mifusa probably wouldn't have been my optimum choice, had the listing been a little more informative. But, based on what I read and how it works, it will do well enough.

The six outlets are too close together for bulky plugs or those that have the transformers built into the plugs. The total amperage across all three USB ports is only 3 amps. So, don't look to power multiple USB devices efficiently. BUT, you CAN plug six AC (that's alternating current, not air conditioning) of a low enough power draw, and three USB powered devices, IF they will all fit in the MIFUSA device, and know that they also have surge protection, as indicated by the little green light.

One star being crap and five stars being spectacular, I rate these as being 'okay'.
text_fidelity_b: Wall Outlet Extender Surge Protector - 6 Outlet Wall Adapter with 3 USB Charging Ports (1 USB-C, 2 USB A), Multi Plug Outlets Wall Mount with Top Phone Holder for Home, Dorm Essentail, 490 Joules

Pioneer Elite SP-EC73 Andrew Jones Home Audio Center Channel Speaker Atmos is the newest (at least at the time of this writing) innovation from Dolby. The idea is, rather than discrete speakers, the system packages sound into objects and has the speakers work together to play the sounds in the way that most recreates what is intended. So in theory you can have as many speakers as you want. In practice, the receivers will support but so many and people will want but so many in their living room. Speakers will always need to have some distance between them or the sounds will blur. The format allows for sound from all directions, including the ceiling and not many people are going to want to hang speakers from the ceiling, which is where a speaker like this comes in.

It has two input pairs, top and bottom. DO NOT plug in the top pair unless your receiver supports Atmos. You can damage it that way. If it does, you put the "upper" speakers into the top pair and these speakers fire upward to bounce the sound off the ceiling giving you the illusion of sound from above.

If you don't yet have Atmos, and you want to pick up great speakers now, and build up over time, you can totally do that with these. You plug in the bottom pair (these will be connected even with Atmos) and let them sit in any speaker position in your configuration. They work well in any standard configuration.

The sound quality is crisp and clear and the range in both pitch and volume is remarkable. The footprint is much smaller than the photo had led me to believe. It looks like an elegant piece of furniture. I love it.

You will need a Philips head screwdriver to put on the base. There are spikes to help balance it on a carpet, but mine lives on a hardwood floor, so I did not attach those.
text_fidelity_b: Pioneer Elite SP-EC73 Andrew Jones Home Audio Center Channel Speaker

text_fidelity_a:
REOLINK 4K Security Camera Outdoor System, Surveillance IP PoE Camera with Human/Vehicle/Pet Detection, 25FPS Daytime, 100F IR Night Vision, Work with Smart Home, Up to 256GB SD Card, RLC-810A Fantastic camera. One of those items that screamed quality right out of the box. Good build, compact size, and has a waterproof connector for your Ethernet cable. Can be mounted where the cable comes through a hole in a fascia board behind the camera or where the cable comes out the side of the base. Base is infinitely adjustable. Camera has slight overhang on the top to keep water off the lens. Three pigtail cables - RJ-45 female connector can be the single cable if you have PoE or you can power this via a 12v power adapter or cable (local or centralized) for versatility.

This is my first IP camera, but I've used many analog cameras and DVRs.

I've hooked this up three ways: By itself, to a switch on the same network as a stand-alone NVR, and to a switch on the same network utilizing my QNAP NAS as the NVR - in each case powered by PoE. Here are some details I've figured out in the process:

---By itself: You can view it quickly and easily without delay with the App, which seems to have all the things you'd expect from a camera viewing app. I assume you can record to or snapshot to an SD card from the description, but I'm going to record to my network, so I didn't try that feature. This was just plug and play, worked super easy.

What I love is that once you figure out the IP address, you can access the camera via a webserver, which pretty much future-proofs the hardware. I despise "smart" devices where you need an app, because then you're at their mercy to run their app on whatever OS they decide to use and they can force you to make accounts, update, etc. Having this open to the user/owner is the way to go. Bravo.

And that web server is full featured. I was able to play around and do everything here before I bothered downloading the app.

Note that - like every camera I've ever used - the viewing software sends a substream which is lower resolution unless you demand the higher resolution. With the app you can see low and medium resolution, but 4k has trouble playing over WiFi (or else it's just smart enough to realize my screen can't support it anyway). Just pointing this out so you realize if you're seeing pixels, that doesn't mean the camera isn't actually recording at 4k.

---With NVR: I recently acquired a cheap 8-channel 4k NVR that I believe to be a Uniview OEM. I added a hard drive and put it on the same network as this camera. The NVR has an 8 port PoE switch built in, but it must also be a router, because it wants to use a different subnet if you put the camera on the NVR's switch. Otherwise, you can easily point the NVR to the camera via IP address.

So...if you point the NVR to the camera via IP address, you can view the camera from its own app or from the NVR app. I assume this still takes one of the NVRs 8 channels. This might be useful if you want to give someone access to just one camera on your network. But it occurred to me that, setup this way, you have constant data streaming over your network, and after you add quite a few cameras in 4k, this is going to start adding up.

If you put the camera directly on the NVR, you'll have to change the IP manually to match the subnet, or maybe you'll somehow get it to work through the NVR or with DHCP. I hadn't bothered spending time figuring this out yet because at the time I thought I'd just use my other switch, but I'm thinking once I get more cameras, it'll probably make more sense to put them directly onto the NVR and ...actually, then I won't have to change my entire IP scheme since I won't have so many new devices to organize.

I'm certain I can get it all working in unison with no problem, but it is more complicated than if you just buy an NVR set with a bunch of cameras already ready to work together. Either way shouldn't be a problem if you have IP knowledge, but I'm guessing a random homeowner might prefer a set.

---Using my NAS as NVR. Hmmm...a little disappointed with QNAP in this regard. I mean, I have three NASs, and I'm assuming they all have 2 licenses included, but to combine them into one program then I believe requires yet another license. I'm not into licenses, even if they're a one time deal, because that means you need accounts and if something happens where they're lost, you can run into all kinds of other issues. I just think consumers need to stand up to this sort of thing. But anyway, I had two included, so I tried it out:

I realized that this is a lot of work for my little consumer grade NAS, and even if I had a more hardcore NAS, I'm not sure I want resources being used all the time. It seems like I couldn't get it to use H.265 compression, nor could I get it to record at the higher resolutions and frame rates. Again, I didn't play with this too awful much once I got it recording and working because I already realized I definitely like the stand alone DVR better. The QNAP even had extra stuff to download and windows to pop up on your PC and all this other stuff. Just not as streamlined as I had hoped.

----Conclusion is that the camera is awesome. I'm not sure many are any better at this point. If you want something that just works easy and you don't know much about networking, you may wish to just buy an NVR set. But if you are IP capable, I think buying components separately could be a great way to go because you can really customize what you want to do. But as always, more options with networking means more potential headaches. But I am pretty certain that once you get it working the way you want it, you should be able to forget all about it and have it work indefinitely.

Oh, and after all that, I shouldn't forget to point out that I'd be thrilled to have this all by itself watching my porch just so I can tell when there's a package out there. My Ring (that came with the house) can't even see that because of the angle it is set at.
text_fidelity_b: REOLINK 4K Security Camera Outdoor System, Surveillance IP PoE Camera with Human/Vehicle/Pet Detection, 25FPS Daytime, 100F IR Night Vision, Work with Smart Home, Up to 256GB SD Card, RLC-810A

Munitio SV Mobile Performance Earphones with 3 Button Mic Control, Bronze Lower and mid end earphones have generally been lacking in both quality and performance. Given my propensity to misplace them, I have been reluctant to invest in more expensive versions. But with increased reliance on mobile devices, it was most definitely time to upgrade.

My familiarity with Munitio was more from their urban chic style complete with bullet motif, Kevlar coated cord, "tactical" carrying case and "hollow point" ear cups. At the risk of looking more Duck dynasty than cool, I was eager to try them.

Designed for use with Apple devices, the phones come securely packaged in a black carrying case. The look is sleek and modern and the bronze color is appealing. These are also available in black and gray. There are three sets of ear cups in different sizes. They were comfortable and shut out outside noise. The cord is flat and tangle free with a heft that promises durability. The 3 button mic control is located on the upper left hand side of the earphone cable. I really couldn't see the buttons but quickly mastered them by touch. They provide full functionality for calls and music on iPods, iPods and iPhones and just music for other mp3 players and Android devices.

I encountered no difficulties in making or taking calls. I could hear the other party and they could hear me without difficulty. The mic is positioned close enough to the mouth and is sufficiently sensitive that I didn't have to scream or repeat things. I made calls from a fairly busy coffee shop and a mall and ambient noise did not impair the call quality.

I tried these earphones with my IPod and a cheap mp3 player of dubious lineage. The sound was clear, strong and enjoyable. I did not find the bass overwhelming and was generally pleased with the performance.

Bottom line, I liked these earphones. The case and the trio of ear cups are thoughtful touches. Although light, there is a sense of substance and quality. The controls are intuitive and easy to use. There is a two year limited warranty. Serving up generous doses of comfort, convenience and performance, these ear phones are right on target.

text_fidelity_a:
ARCTIC Breeze Pro USB Desktop Fan with 4-Port USB Hub This review covers two different models of the Arctic fan:

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>Model with USB hub:
I have been using the original ARCTIC Breeze for a while and have been very pleased with its performance, and especially pleased with how quiet it runs. The Pro model builds on that and adds a few more useful features.

Unlike the original model which had a bendable stem with a USB plug on the end, the Pro has a base so the fan can be positioned away from the USB port on the PC. The attached power cord is a little over 5 feet long, making it possible to put the fan on my desk and plug it into the PC on the floor.

The base also has 4 USB input ports, so it works as a USB hub. It has a 5V power input jack if you want to turn this into an active hub. The power adapter to do so is NOT included.

Unlike the single-speed original version, this has a knob so you can vary the speed. It's not precise, but there is a somewhat noticeable difference between low and high. It's a continually variable speed - you can turn the dial to whatever speed you like.

Best of all, it's just as quiet, if not quieter, than the original model. That's the biggest plus for me by far, since the cheap USB fans make a racket. This just makes a low-pitched hum. The build quality is solid - the base is sturdy, and the bendable arm holds its position well.

One negative: the packaging. It's in a clam shell package that is a major, major pain to open!

While it's more expensive than the original, the added benefits of being able to position it on a desk and use it as a hub makes the upgrade worth considering. Highly recommend.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>USA EDITION:
I've have (and use) a couple other Arctic USB fans and have been 100% satisfied with them. This new version (their "USA Edition") has a couple of improvements over past designs.

The base is a metal plate which increases the fan's stability when you're bending the stem to point the fan. The on/off/speed dial switch no longer has a lit LED ring around it. I never found the lit LED ring to be bothersome on the other Arctic fans, so having or not having it is not a big deal to me.

The base also does away with the USB hub connections that other models have. That's keeps the base more streamlined and allows it to have a lower profile. It also does away with the clam shell packaging, instead using a very easy to open box.

The build quality of this, like the other Arctic fans I have, is excellent. The stem is bendy by stays put where you want it; the operating sound is pretty hushed; the on/off/speed control works well. The overall design is attractive, with a red/white/blue color scheme and graphics.

It moves a surprising amount of air. No, it won't blow your hair back as a Vornado fan will, but this makes a noticeable difference in circulating air. The size makes it very easy to find a spot on your desk to position it.

While I can't speak to the long-term reliability of this as of yet, I expect it will last for some time. I have an Arctic fan similar to this that I've been using almost daily for the past 1+ years, and it still works as good as it did when new.

Looks good, works well, and easy to use. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: ARCTIC Breeze Pro USB Desktop Fan with 4-Port USB Hub

text_fidelity_a:
Mostof Dual Ring Light with Stand, Mirror, Phone Holder, Remote, for TikTok YouTube Live Stream Makeup Selfie Photography So ... 2020 .... what do you think of it so far? Our meetings for worship have been moved to Zoom online. So we are are video conferencing multiple times a week. The lighting in our office and on my Mac is great. But for those meetings we use my husband's window's based, 5 year old laptop, out in the kitchen because it runs one of the secondary programs we need to use. The lighting is just "meh". I have been trying to find a good lighting source and have tried and returned a few products out of my own pocket.

This system is a keeper. I little cumbersome, a little top heavy, a little cheap feeling in some respects, but lighting wise, when you get it adjusted is quite nice. Us personally, we look a little more like real people with better lighting.

I have included a before and after picture. I am not a selfie taker, just a pushing 50 year old, middle aged woman, so bear with my picture, I just tried to give you an idea of what some light and color adjustments can do.

Ours is set with a red filter. That seemed to work best for our laptop camera. It is set to medium brightness. Ours is extended over us with the round lights facing more downward and out of our eyes. They are positioned more over the laptop than near us and maybe a foot above the laptop. There is more play for extension with the unit, but that is what works for us.

It comes with mirrors and phone holders, etc etc. We don't use any of that right now but it gives you options. The round mirror head which the the two lights screw on to is flimsy. I would not be surprised if it breaks eventually. The weight of the lights on the small screw in assembly just don't seem like someone thought this all the way through with gravity and weight. So be forewarned. That could be improved.

Overall ... finally a lighting system that works and is pretty simple to set up. Any regrets? Actually no! Would I recommend? Yes. This definitely has a place in today's zoom, tiktok, instagram, youtubey saavy world of Influencers, and also for those of us joe-schmoes who just need better lighting.
text_fidelity_b: Mostof Dual Ring Light with Stand, Mirror, Phone Holder, Remote, for TikTok YouTube Live Stream Makeup Selfie Photography

text_fidelity_a:
REOLINK Security Camera Outdoor, Wireless Rechargable Battery Powered, 1080P Starlight Night Vision, PIR Motion Video for Home Surveillance (1 Pack) The camera quality is fine and live viewing through the app is fine (Android version anyway). What is TERRIBLE: Security camera features. Bottom of the barrel. There is a sensitivity to motion slider for when the camera starts, but that is ALL. No way of mapping out areas you want to ignore (e.g sidewalk or pets). "Free" cloud is a rippoff. You get 8 SECOND highly compressed clips!! That's it. If you store locally on an SD card you can get up to 30 seconds.

If you want this camera for security monitoring, unless 8 second snippets work for you, look elsewhere. You can't even pay them to get longer recordings. Since I bought this thing because of the free cloud service, I consider this a total ripoff. Dishonest.

Through the windows app: The settings are confusing. The interface is awful. You can't set it to automatically open a live view. Instead you have to open & click on an icon. You can't leave it in live view (it will automatically shut off after a little while "to save battery." Isn't that my choice? I should be able to use the battery if I want to. I like to leave the live view open when I'm expecting someone.

I would not buy this again. Look to the real brands like linksys, Nest, Ring, etc. if you actually want a security camera and not a little toy.
text_fidelity_b: REOLINK Security Camera Outdoor, Wireless Rechargable Battery Powered, 1080P Starlight Night Vision, PIR Motion Video for Home Surveillance (1 Pack)

Belkin 8-Outlet Surge Protector with Power Cord Organizer, Designed for Office and Conference Room I have a huge Belkin surge protector in my office that meets all of my needs and also occasionally makes me lunch (it's pretty rad), but since having a baby, I've found that my definition of "rad" has changed to mean not visible, attractive, or accessible by the baby. While this isn't meant to be babyproof, I've found that the cage-like design and locking mechanism not only keep my cords tidier, but also makes them a lot less obvious and exciting to baby so that when it is placed out of reach, he isn't always clamoring to be lifted up to it, as he does with high-up cords that are not as hidden.

Two things that I don't love: One is that the sliding mechanism that opens out to allow you to put the cords in and use the diagonally-sliding plugs easily - they are a little stiff. So stiff that in fact I doubted whether I was really supposed to slide them out and was afraid I'd break the thing. I also found the locking/ opening/ closing mechanism too stiff - in fact, I gashed my finger when it opened unexpectedly after having to push it harder than I should have to open it.

The other thing is that there is no method for hanging this outlet on the wall. So I have to set it on a high shelf, which is less cool than just hanging it behind my printer or something.

Otherwise, I love that I can neaten up a decidedly un-neat portion of my office with this, and be assured of clean power to boot.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin 8-Outlet Surge Protector with Power Cord Organizer, Designed for Office and Conference Room

Jabra Evolve 65t True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds, UC Optimized – Superior Call Quality and Connectivity – Passive Noise Cancelling Earbuds with up to 15 hours of Battery Life with Charging Case These headphones are advertised more for business use than for music. The business features do work great. There is a bluetooth adapter included in the package so you can use the headphones with PCs that don't have built-in bluetooth. You can connect the headphones to 2 different bluetooth sources simultaneously so you can have a Skype call on your laptop and connect to your smartphone at the same time. There is a nice pass-through mode that lets you listen to your surroundings (or not) by pushing a button on the Jabra app.

Speaking of the app, the included manual is very skimpy and really unnecessary. To use these headphones you should download the Jabra app to your phone or PC and use the app to pair and configure the headphones. Many of the features are only available through the app.

Sound quality of the headphone is great for business use, very solid with no connection problems. For music, this is not the best I have heard from "true wireless" headphones. Some music-focused "true wireless" headphones that I own have better clarity and detail. The Jabra app does have an equalizer feature, but the effect is more subtle than what I get from other headphones.

These headphones are very comfortable and very secure, actually surprisingly secure for headphones that don't have any wings or clips. 3 different size ear tips are included, though no memory foam tips like you get with some headphones in this price range.

Battery life is 5 hours per charge and you can recharge twice with the included carrying case. That's good for "true wireless" headphones.

I would give these headphones 5 stars if the sound quality was better. It does have good business features and those are the main focus of this product. Bluetooth connection is very solid and build quality is great. 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Evolve 65t True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds, UC Optimized – Superior Call Quality and Connectivity – Passive Noise Cancelling Earbuds with up to 15 hours of Battery Life with Charging Case

The design provides a stable center of gravity that allows it to securely hold devices up to 10" size in vertical or horizontal mode. I tested it with my iPad 4, a Kindle Fire HD, and an iPhone and found they all securely fit into the groove with or without cases on.

This stand adjusts from flat against the back to an angle that would have your device flat like a table top and all points in between. It has a silicon lined groove that holds your device securely as well as silicon contact points to protect your device from scratches. It also has four anti-slip silicon pads on the bottom of the stand that protect the surface you set it on.

This stand makes doing work on my iPad so much easier than using it laying flat. I can set it up on my desk or a table, run the power cord through the opening in the base and out through the back to charge it, and slide a Bluetooth keyboard over the stand's base. I also like experimenting with recipes I find online when I cook and I like being able to see the recipe better when it's on this stand. It's also very useful to get my iPad up off the counter in case I spill something too.

More and more schools assign homework that requires an iPad or other device, so this stand is very useful for studying. It's lightweight enough to move around effortlessly, but doesn't fold up flat so it is not convenient to take when traveling. This is a very well made stand that useful and convenient for home, school, or office use though, so I'd gladly recommend it for those uses.

Item provided by Omoton for my evaluation and review. I hope that my inspection and observations about it prove helpful in your decision making.

text_fidelity_a:
Jiusion Telescope Eyepiece Plossl Eyepiece 32mm with 1.25inch Filter Threaded, Astronomical Telescope Lens 50% FOV increase at this price? This is the lowest priced Plössl I've ever seen and the reason for choosing it. Curiosity.

As a physicist with a too time-consuming career to fool around with optical Garage-a-Tronics projects, it's time for fun. After >40 years, I'd guess 1/3 of my time was in electro-optical systems. My responsibilities included one of the nation's most sophisticated optical design, fabrication, and 50-200 layers of Å thickness vapor deposition coating capability (200 layers is no limit … simply the most I've seen engineered)

You have to give them credit. Chinese optics are extraordinary and have been for 20 years. Asian pricing has wholly changed the marketplace. The crazy low prices have made complex systems affordable to the mass market. Optical grinding facilities remaining in the US are confined to a handful of custom, proto-typing houses run by old-timers with a decidedly different product application than consumer use.

The Plössl eyepiece is quite expensive to manufacture given the nature of the glass, coatings, and its precisely coordinated concave and convex lenses to neutralize internal reflections.

The Plössl has tradeoffs. All optical systems do. For example, Plössl's increased FOV comes with an eye relief confined to 70–80% of focal length.

Lenses are analog. Performance is not binary. 'Lowest price' in optics might be misunderstood. Optics lots begin production targeted at a spec performance that makes a profit. A production lot will yield a normal distribution to spec. On the upper end of the distribution are a few 'blue diamonds' commanding a super premium. Theoretically, 66%, will meet the target spec. Production lots begin life as profitable, spec-centered customers. 7% would be expected to fall short of some spec performance (i.e. start 107% of what you need) … Harvard MBA's demanding perfection in all things except stock value have never come to terms with normal analog distributions in scientific endeavors.

The lenses come without ref to detail specs, so I would believe the factory is emptying the shelves of sub-spec product here. Spec fallout, in my experience, may have little or nothing to do with operator perceptions of performance.

Excellent fun.

Was my review helpful? If so, click "Helpful" so I can know. Trying hard to put integrity into reviews
text_fidelity_b: Jiusion Telescope Eyepiece Plossl Eyepiece 32mm with 1.25inch Filter Threaded, Astronomical Telescope Lens

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th) If you want a 10" tablet for reading books and watching videos/TV shows/movies and can't afford more money than this (price regularly drops to $100), then this is good product choice. Performance is fine for e-books and videos, but sometimes sluggish for intense game playing, photo/video editing or even text editing. The SD card slot lets you store lots of TV shows and movies and use the main memory for apps (which often work poorly if stored on the SD card). Kindle e-books sometimes work much better on the Fire tablets than on ipads or Android tablets, especially if the books have embedded audio or video. The user interface revolves around the books and videos that you bought from Amazon. With a considerable amount of work, you may be able to replace the user interface with a more standard Android launcher that focuses on your apps and files. Realistically, the performance of this tablet clunky enough that I don't recommend it unless you are mostly using it for e-books and videos, so maybe changing the user interface is not worth the effort.

You should also ask yourself if you are using the tablet for mostly e-books and videos, do you really need a 10 inch screen? The 8 inch Kindle Fire tablet has similar performance and a much lower price and is also lighter weight and less bulky, making it easier to use in many situations.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th)

text_fidelity_a:
Zmodo Pivot 1080p 360° Rotating Wireless Security Camera and All-in-One Smart Home Hub No Sensor Included Unboxing: Two circles of tape, one at each end of a printed box sheath. Good quality plain blue box underneath with Zmodo logo. The presentation is nice enough to make it a good gift, without veering into making you pay for packaging. Within are cord, window/door sensors, and device, all well protected for shipping. Device is black, but cords and window sensors are all white. Protective film of plastic over the lens.

The device itself is about the diameter of a coffee cup, but with an aspect more like a drink can. It's a mix of matte black and a shiny black that attracts lint like a magnet.
Three rubber feet raise it above the table. A speaker is inset underneath. Made in China. Model number is on the bottom. It feels like a good quality device. There is a chemical smell, but I think it's coming from the instructions, not the camera. The power socket is ungrounded wall outlet to MicroUSB, which is a bit tired, but at least very common and compatible. I wish Europe would reduce their regulations enough to assist the adoption of USB C.

Plugged it in. The ring on top lights up green and blinks. Then the camera pans around once and has a look around.

Downloaded and installed the Zmodo app, which has really polarized reviews and needs access to:
Device and App history
Identity
Contacts
Location
SMS
Phone
Photos/Media/Files
Camera
Microphone
Wifi connection
Device ID and Call information
I can see why the needs permissions for most of that, but it is still a lot of access if anyone were in a position to abuse it.

Opened the app, gave it an email address and password to create an account.

Clicked Add Device, then Wireless Device.

Clicked the check mark twice, and then entered WiFi password.

Waited while things blinked for about a minute. Ring changed from green flashy, to blue flashy, to blue solid. Camera has another look around and does some clicking.

Named the device and gave it a password.

Clicked on the still image that looked like it came from the camera and was into the live feed, displayed on my Android smart phone (Galaxy S6). Clicking on the arrows on either side of the screen turns the camera. apparently, it can see in any direction, but once it gets to a certain point, it needs to turn around and go the other way, it can't just keep spinning.

Thus far, everything seems to be working except the motion tracking, which was kind of the main selling point. I have it turned on in phone settings. Looking at their support pages, it seems that it won't motion track once you gave been in the room a while. They recommended I leave the room for 10 minutes and come back so that the microwave array will find me interesting again. Also, apparently you can view your feed on a computer by logging in on their website.

After leaving for ten minutes and then returning to the room and sitting near it, it took about a minute for it to notice something was amiss, at which point it did a slow scan of the whole room and snapped a picture of me when it saw me move. It then stopped, still looking in the wrong direction.

My end verdict is that it's actually quite a bit nicer than previous wifi cameras I've tested, but falls far short of what I would like to see in a motion tracking camera. The motion tracking is slow and dense, when it works at all. There are enough additional features, like using as a speaker, communicating with someone through it, temperature and humidity data, etc, to give it a more versatile set of uses, but without the motion detection/control being solid, it all feels thrown together and tacked on.

I received a sample for review but opinions are my own.
text_fidelity_b: Zmodo Pivot 1080p 360° Rotating Wireless Security Camera and All-in-One Smart Home Hub No Sensor Included

text_fidelity_a:
Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black Update: I have now tried two other brands (a coworker's, and bought another brand) of ergonomic mice that both work substantially better than the Anker version, which also cost less! I highly suggest anyone considering buying this, skip over it and look for another one that is cheaper with good reviews. It amazes me that a company with a known name can skip out on quality so much that other product that cost half as much outperform it in every way.

The Good:
Feels great to hold. More natural than a typical mouse. All the buttons are in the right places and do not require any strain to press. The wheel is in the perfect spot to be used by my middle finger, which is typically what I try to do, since I swear I already have arthritis in my point finger being under 30 years old...

The Bad: There is an obvious input delay, making this pretty terrible for anyone who grew up using computers. That no one else has mentioned this is beyond me. Side by side comparison of any of my Logitech mice and this Anker mouse makes the input delay on this mouse even more obvious. It feels like trying to use a mouse on a TV with interpolation (120 Hz, smooth motion, etc.) enabled. On top of the nearly deal-breaking latency issue, the input into the computer is inconsistent, causing the mouse to frequently skip around or miss my movements.

If you expect to play any game that requires any amount of precision or is time-based, you will regret buying this mouse. Games aside, this mouse reduces my productivity because of how unreliable the signal is, and the extra effort needed to predict the movement of the cursor due to the lag.

I tried the wired version of this mouse (a friend had it) and the input lag is not as bad, but is still there. Therefore, I advise against anyone buying this or the wired version, and suggest to instead look elsewhere.
text_fidelity_b: Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black

text_fidelity_a: Arlo VMC4030-100NAR PRO Add-on Camera, White (Renewed) I received my Arlo Pro ahead of the delivery schedule. It was packaged nicely/professionally even though it is refurbished & came with charging/mounting accessories. I already have 3 Arlo cameras from before and wanted to add an additional camera and read that the Arlo Pro worked more efficiently than the Arlo 2. I struggled the first night setting it up (otherwise a very fast system to set up). I had placed it in a window which prohibited the motion device, so I ended up mounting it outside (and I do purchase the silicon skins to protect my devices) with the suggestion of Tech support and it works beautifully now (tech support wait time was less than 2 minutes on a Sunday afternoon/PST). At first, the camera appeared to have a glitch with a constant flashing, so I removed the battery and reinserted it and it was fine. Tech support was able to remote into my cameras to test whether it was getting Wifi, optimized settings, signals, etc. which was very helpful in figuring out where I was having my issue. Video is in color; it records sounds excellently; AND has a mic which I haven't accessed yet. All added features can be customized or turned off altogether (i.e., sound). In trying to set up my Pro, I watched a few Arlo videos which introduced me to the "MODE" tab option which then allowed me to access ALL my cameras in customizing my cameras better than just going straight into DEVICE tab. Not confirmed, but I think the MODE overrides any settings that you would do to your device if you go directly into DEVICE tab. Select MODE tab, then select your BASE, then click on your cameras individually & SAVE. Having accessed the MODE, ALL my cameras are now working much better. I get email alerts (which is set under MODE & can be turned off if you wish). I have had my Arlo system since 2016 and with my new addition, can't beat the price and reliability of the device. However, I do clean the lenses periodically for optimum motion detection. I do like that the Arlo Pro is rechargeable because my other 3 are not and it costs me about $40 in batteries every 3 months (those cameras take 4 batteries each).  If you find video you want to save, you can download it to your PC/Smart Phone for safe keeping; otherwise, Arlo Cloud clears your video library on the 7th day (which comes with the camera free with the option to subscribe to Arlo if you want a longer history). Bottom-line, you can purchase this system and grow it to meet your needs and upgrade cameras to which the base will support it. I can access https://arlo.netgear.com/#/login via PC or SmartPhone to view my LIBRARY. I do recommend updating your phone app periodically.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo VMC4030-100NAR PRO Add-on Camera, White (Renewed)

LG Cinema Screen 55LM8600 55-Inch Cinema 3D 1080p 240Hz Dual Core LED-LCD HDTV with Smart TV and Six Pairs of 3D Glasses (2012 Model) The picture is astounding. A few friends and I watched [[ASIN:B004K4N64E Tron: Legacy / Tron: The Original Classic (Five-Disc Combo: Blu-ray 3D / Blu-ray / DVD / Digital Copy)]] on this, and althought I love the movie, I couldn't pay attention to the movie the first time through. I was too busy staring in awe at the way the clouds in the distant background moved, or the beauty of the image. I was told passive 3D is an image quality drop from HD because it projects half the image to each eye, but I'm calling that theory out. This picture is glorious.

When it upscales images to 3D it can get a little odd. I watched Naruto on it, and some moments were astounding, and some were just odd, as Naruto's eyes seemed to deepen into layers. Overall, I like the upscale. It's an approximation of 3D, but it's a darn good approximation.

My boyfriend wears huge glasses and these fit over them perfectly. On a lark, I put them on over my largest sunglasses, and they still fit, so if you wear glasses, even very large glasses, and you have any concerns that they won't work well with these, stop worrying.

As to connectors, there is one input for composite in, but it comes with a three-into-one adapter for that. The same for component in. Those are the only cable that come with it, so you will need those. I suggest [[ASIN:B003L1ZYYW AmazonBasics High-Speed HDMI Cable (9.8 Feet/3.0 Meters) - Supports Ethernet, 3D, and Audio Return [Newest Standard]]] as they are reliable and implement 3D transmission well. There are four specifications for HDMI, 1.4 being the latest, and not every device or cable fully implements the specification. The signal will downgrade to the lowest component, and with a TV like this, you don't want that component to be your cable. The difference is substantial.

There are four HDMI ports, and it doesn't seem to like connecting to an HDMI switcher. If you have a lot of devices plugged in, and you often find yourself wondering which input the DVD player is using, you'll love this. First, if a device isn't actively sending a signal, it displays as greyed out, and moves to the back of the list. Second, you can name your inputs. You select them from a list (I would have likes to call one Playstation 2, but had to opt for "Game") but it helps a lot.

The remote is kind of like a Wii controller. You wave it around and it points at things on the screen you can select. Very cute. If you find it hard to use, back up a few steps. It's counterintuitive, but it works. The cursor slows down.

For streaming it has the standard YouTube, Netflix and Hulu among others. The only tiny downside is that it doesn't yet support Amazon on demand videos. Plug in a [[ASIN:B005CLPP84 Roku 2 XS 1080p Streaming Player]] and you're set for streaming entertainment. I am in the process of replacing my router. It's in such bad shape that my Pingtest results range from B- to C when connected wirelessly. Whatever caching the set top does, it can provide perfect clarity even in such adverse conditions. Good to know if your Internet can have "off moments".

The energy star note that came on the TV (the yellow tag required by law that you see on all appliances these days) claims that this TV will have an Estimated Yearly Energy Cost of $14 with a range for similar models (45" - 49" TVs) going from $18 to $51. This is "Based on 11 cents per kWh and 5 hours use per day."

I wish I could give this 50 stars. It's perfect.
text_fidelity_b: LG Cinema Screen 55LM8600 55-Inch Cinema 3D 1080p 240Hz Dual Core LED-LCD HDTV with Smart TV and Six Pairs of 3D Glasses (2012 Model)

text_fidelity_a:
Skullcandy Crusher ANC Personalized Noise Canceling Wireless Headphone - Black Hands down the best headphones I've ever put on for bass. I ran them through my audio tester and these picked up way lower tones than my Senn's which have been my long standing pair for bass. It does seem to come at that cost of picking up the higher notes, but honestly when pitches are that high, they are annoying and I'm fine with the headphones not picking them up. I don't need to hear a dog whistle...

Mid-range was true, sound was immersive, the headset was light and comfortable. A bit warm on the ears but pretty much all closed style headsets are.
So why the three stars?
OMG the constant never ending hissing. Unless you are playing something loud enough to cover it up, it is always there. Even when I turned off ANC, even when I switched to ambient mode. HIIIISSSSSSSSSSSSS. I tried to ignore it but it was always there. I work on the computer and sometimes I have to hear audio tracks and othertimes there is silence, I have to physically remove these every time I am not playing something or HIIIIISSSSSSSSSSSSSS. Honestly have no idea how other reviews aren't bothered by this, its the loudest hissing static I've ever heard coming through headsets.

If you are like me and do not have sound coming out the entire time you are wearing them, do not buy. They will make you insane with rage, RAAWWRRR.

If you are only going to wear them while listening to music, and want the best bass you can find, buy these they are AMAZING for that, seriously. But ugh that hissing.
text_fidelity_b: Skullcandy Crusher ANC Personalized Noise Canceling Wireless Headphone - Black

NIXGIR UNL A1 True Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.3 Headphones with ENC Microphone, HiFi Stereo Sound, 18H Playtime, IPX4 Waterproof Okay, so price to satisfaction ratio is one way to define the products' quality. It is really not expensive yet not so excellent either. So here is what I think.

Build Quality / Design: it's small and very conventional Bluetooth earbuds design, so looks very similar to Air Pods. Build quality is not so bad for its price and I have no complain about this part. The matt brushed finish does look pretty fancy but I don't know why they leaved some part unbrushed. So some part looks pretty nice but some look like just plastic. Yet, since it is $14, so I don't think I should complain so much.

Sound Quality : I am not so sure about this part. This does have all the functions which earbuds should have (touch control, voice calling etc) but it simply lacks the depth of the sound. It sounds like slightly improved version of Air plane bundle earphone, so not worth to discuss about base/mid/high range. For sound quality, something is off in the sound quality.

Ergonomics: So this one has old Air Pods design, you cannot change the soft rubber to adjust the size to fit your years. After few hours of use, I felt uncomfortableness and slight pain with this ear phone but I have small ear and I feel pain with Air Pods as well, so my opinion is not so important for this matter I guess.

Buy if you are looking for : some quick substitute for your Galaxy Buds / Air Pods / or other ear buds and price is very important for your purchase decision. Interestingly, this earbuds mic is weirdly good.

Don't if you are looking for : earbuds with excellent sound quality / very comfortable fit

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EF 100mm f/2.8L IS USM Macro Lens with UV Protection Lens Filter The Canon 100mm f/2.8 USM macro is a lovely lens already, and Canon would need to significantly improve on it to make any owner of this lens consider selling in order to upgrade to the new L version. The new Canon 100mm f/2.8 L USM macro lens with image stabilization fits the bill and this particular 100mm macro owner, at least, decided to upgrade. I rented this lens at first to try out the new features, as my older 100mm lens is one of my most-coveted, most-used lenses, and I didn't want to give up on it simply because there was a new kid on the block. After the instant rebates came around I was in a well-enough informed position to make the purchase, and at a good price.

The aforementioned Image Stabilization is very effective in situations where you can't use the tripod, but want to maintain critical focus while working with shallow depth of field. The IS system in this lens, to boot, is an improvement on Canon's IS system found in other earlier lenses - Hybrid IS, a system which is particularly tuned to the demands of macro photography; I've tested this with the new lens and it's amazing what I can successfully capture handheld that previously absolutely necessitated a tripod. You can get the same results handheld now with approximately 3-4 less stops of light than you could previously. This perfectly suits my shooting style - I like to roam around, usually sans tripod, and take images in natural surroundings that may not always have the best available light. A relatively slow shutter speed to capture the scene in front of me usually meant I'd have to compensate by ratcheting up the ISO or go wider with the aperture, which are not always or often good compromises, for image quality reasons as well as for reasons of creative choice. The IS is a much welcome feature, and provides more leeway in variable lighting. Also sometimes people complain that the IS is too noisy when in operation; while that can certainly be true (I have a couple of other Canon lenses with IS), I have found that the new IS system in this latest lens is noticeably quieter - I'd call it pretty quiet, even with nothing else to compare it to.

Out of focus highlights - the bokeh - is smooth, smoother than the older version. Images appear very crisp, I'm pleased with the sharpness. The new lens is about an ounce or so heavier than the older one, not so much that you'd really notice. Also the lens, while a L, does not have the same build appearance as other L lenses - it is not hefty and metallic, and cream-colored. That doesn't bother me so much, but others more invested in the distinctive look of Canon L lenses might care. The lens body itself is sleek (compared to the rather portly older model) and has a nice matte black finish which you can handle easily - I don't quite know how to describe it - it doesn't have the usual "slippery" metal feel to it, so you don't feel like you might drop it if you aren't careful. Because it's an L, it comes with a lens hood; I always get hoods for my lenses, so I love it when a lens has one included!

One thing that is an interesting feature is that there are three settings for the Autofocus limiter (the older lens has two). It's basically there to help speed the AF in finding its optimal focus depending on which camera-to-subject distance you are shooting with - anywhere from strictly close up (.3 to .5 meter of distance) to full range. I'm still trying to figure out what real time difference it makes to choose between the .3m-to-infinity limiter and .5m-to-infinity limiter, but I assume it must make some difference for Canon to have included the additional option. Early days yet, I'll figure it out.

All in all - not every lens redesign results in a lens worth ditching an old model for, especially when the upgrade entails a bit more cost. But the new 100mm macro L is very much worth the upgrade, and the IS is a welcome addition to Canon's most popular macro option. Now if they'll just put IS in the 180mm...

I will also add that I made this particular purchase through the Marketplace seller J&R. I had no problems with them - delivery was swift and the item was well-packed.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF 100mm f/2.8L IS USM Macro Lens with UV Protection Lens Filter

text_fidelity_a:
Rosewill 3.5 Inch Hard Drive Enclosure to USB 3.0 / eSATA. External Hard Drive Case Aluminum Body, Built-in Cooling Fan and Fan Switch. Support 3.5” SATA III / II / I Hard Drive up to 6TB and UASP function. Wouldn't recognize on the eSATA port. It would detect the HDD, but would not format nor store data. I thought it would be plug and play. I submitted a return request (which the seller approved), but after extensive Googling, discovered how to make it work on my machine.

1) For Windows 7 (I think Windows 10 may not have this issue), make sure you have the registry entry to allow AHCI.
2) In BIOS, make sure your boot devices are in proper order.
3) In BIOS, update RAID configuration to AHCI.

text_fidelity_a:
Lowepro Passport Sling DSLR Camera Bag I was looking for a sling camera bag for ease of use when I am in action mode, e.g., hanging off the side of a jeep during safari, hanging over the railing of a boat while photographing breaching whales. I did not want the typical backpack or the shoulder bag (both of which I own) that would impede me from such movements and/or would need to be set down while I was shooting.

I like to leave my zoom lens on my camera. I attach a lens in the open as few times as possible for the obvious reasons, e.g., salt air, dust. I have a Nikon 200-500 lens attached to a D4 body. With that configuration, the camera/lens is 14.25" long, D4 body is 6" wide and lens at its widest is 5" and it fills this bag's length (including the unzipped 30% extra). That set up is also about 10-11 pounds of weight. However, in order to fit it . . . I had to remove the square cushioned "cube" that is affixed by velcro into one side of the bag. Once my cameras/lens was in the bag, there was about 3" of horizontal (lengthwise space) left and 3" of vertical space as well as small pockets of space around the camera/lens itself. I would not be able to fit my IPad. I could probably tuck my IPhone in somewhere. Extra batteries, battery charger and cords would be doubtful. One extra battery perhaps.

The zipper on the top can be zipped either way (which I like). There are cords on the zippers as well for easy grabbing. The "open" pockets on the outside are nice, and while they are 6" deep, there isn't much that has any value that I would store there . . . because the risk of it falling out would be too great. (At least for me . . . because I plan to sling the sling quite a bit). It is difficult to believe that the inside of this bag only has 2 very small pockets. Both pockets have flaps that velcro. One pocket is 4"d x 3"w and the other is 4"d x 2"w. While that seems like a lot . . . the pockets are sewn into the bag and some of that width is lost to the stitching. They are immediately adjacent to each other and immediately under the top zipper (not the most optimum place to be IMHO).

The strap is nice and sturdy and reminds me of my Nikon strap. What I also like is that instead of having the typical strap tightener (don't recall the technical term, but like a buckle), this strap has a cam lock buckle. It is a buckle clip that clips down with pressure on the strap. It will take you less time to adjust your strap, which might not be a big deal to some . . . if you don't adjust your strap very often. Loaded it down with approximately 12 pounds of equipment, slung it on my back and tested it by moving around for a while today . . . and it stayed put. Hopefully, it will do the same when in the field. Strap has 6" wide removable cushion that velcros into place. I will probably double that with another one to make it super comfy. I am 6'0" tall. With the strap over my left shoulder (and the bag sitting on my right hip) and the strap completely extended . . . the top of the bag (where it zips open), is approximately 25" vertically from my right shoulder.

Canvas feels heavyweight. It feels like it might be waxed (and therefore water resistant), but after a bit of due diligence, I cannot find anything that would confirm same. But, you could sling this over your shoulder under a rain jacket or poncho if necessary.

The color is just right for safari (bright colors, whites, greys and/or blacks are frowned upon). This is the main reason why I did not purchase the Passport II or III . . . no natural color choices.

I would describe myself as an intermediate amateur photographer and it has become my hobby in retirement. I live for nature action shots.

I am keeping this bag. I am going to cut off one side of the cushioned "cube" to make a cushioned "U". The open end of the "U" will face up. I will place the camera in the bag so that the cushioned U will cradle my large lens with my camera attached. While it doesn't hold as much as I would like . . . I liken it to a wristlet wallet. It holds exactly what I need at the time I need it. I will still have my camera backpack with me (to hold extra batteries, lenses and the like) and my hubby usually volunteers for carry duty - lucky me! I would like to have given it 5 stars . . . but I feel as though the design needs improvement (the II and III are about the same in size etc.). Unfortunately, this also seems to be the only true sling bag on the market. (My definition of sling is worn like a crossbody with the bag on your back instead of in front).

Look forward to breaking it in very soon.
text_fidelity_b: Lowepro Passport Sling DSLR Camera Bag

Masione 4 Pack Outdoor Fake/Dummy Security Camera with 30 Illuminating LED Light (Silver) CCTV Surveillance [[VIDEOID:ecbfab27d25a92fd322c831d655b23cd]] UPDATED REVIEW 09/25/17:
... apparently they looked SO realistic someone stole the camera itself, lol. I bet they were surprised when they got it home. These still did the trick for awhile at least. I have yet to replace the stolen one, but they are a good deterrent.

ORIGINAL REVIEW
of discounted product

I have had these a couple of months now. I purchased these because we had some mail stolen out of our mailbox. We live on a larger parcel of property and the main gate is a ways from the main house. We are building a package drop box, but until then I needed something more immediate.

I realize someone, upon close inspection will know these are fake, but sometimes a good deterrent is all one needs. I attached these near a power source so it would at least kind of look real. I also put a fake antennae of my own nearby so it would look like it was transmitting wirelessly. I put some electrical tape here and there to make it look like wires running. It was a quick attempt, but for me, it will at least make someone think twice. I will eventually put a game camera out there, more hidden, so then the dummy camera will take the attention off the real camera.

So $5/each for these hulls is not a bad retail price. You add (4) AA batteries and it lights it up at night with an 'infrared" so it looks more real. The infrared is motion sensitive and seems to work well. The top cover slides on to protect the batteries and that too seems to work well.

These were exactly what I was looking for. I searched these out specifically. Until we can afford real cameras that work wirelessly, that far from our house, these deterrents will have to do.

I find no cons with these during the several weeks I have had them in my possession. No regrets.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech HD Pro Webcam C920, Widescreen Video Calling and Recording, 1080p Camera, Desktop or Laptop Webcam (Discontinued by manufacturer) I was able to do a direct side-by-side comparison between three Logitech webcams: the C920, C615, and C525. Here is what I found:

Right away I noticed that the C920 was a superior product - as it should be, considering it is Logitech's flagship webcam at the moment. But my initial impression was that the extra features might not be worth the size and setup tradeoff. There are three things that the C920 does not have:

1) While all three models attach to your computer monitor in about the same way and all three can tilt up and down, only the C525 and C615 can turn side to side. In fact, they can turn around 360 degrees and more. The C920, however, has a threaded tripod mount, as does the C615.

2) The C920 lacks the excellent "fold-and-go" design of the other two models, which makes packing and travelling easy, while protecting the lenses. In contrast, the C920 is much larger and stationary.

3) The C615 comes with a shorter USB cable AND an extension for more versatility. The C920 - like the C525 - comes with only a full length cable (~6'). My wish for all three models is that they come with a detachable USB cable, which would make them all much more portable and easy to carry around, especially in this age when most people travel with at least one or two USB cables.

But when I actually sat down to do some serious comparisons, I realized just how much more advanced the C920 is, most notably in its use of H.264 compression and its autofocus feature.

H.264 is a standard being utilized more and more for video of all sorts, and it makes a huge difference here. Having used all three webcams on the same computer and with the same software, the C920 compresses 1080p video completely while recording and takes about 49MB per 1 minute of recording on the highest settings (720p for one minute takes about 31MB). That uses *.mp4 format.

Meanwhile, the C615 and C525 use *.wmv format and take 99MB and 44MB for one minute of video at 1080p and 720p, respectively. The real problem, though, is that you then have to sit and wait for the video to compress if you are working in 1080.

If you're interested, The C920 has 1 zoom level at 1080 and 4 levels at 720. The C615 has 0 zoom levels at 1080 and about 10 at 720. The C525 has about 10 at 720. All can be used during recording, but the quality involved with the C920 is again far superior.

Also, the autofocus is much better on the C920, with less flickering and light change. You can really get up close and show off your pores and beard growth.

In conclusion, the optics and hardware of the C920 are obviously superior to the others, which are already high quality. If I am using the webcam while highly mobile, then I may opt for one of the others - I might even just settle for the C525 because it's a tiny bit smaller than the C615 and I believe you cannot use the C615 to make 1080p video calling, even if your hotel's Internet service could keep up with the data rate. However, if I am using a webcam at a stationary computer, or am really a videophile, then I definitely want the bigger workhorse.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech HD Pro Webcam C920, Widescreen Video Calling and Recording, 1080p Camera, Desktop or Laptop Webcam (Discontinued by manufacturer)

Neewer 48 Macro LED Ring Flash Bundle with LCD Display Power Control, Adapter Rings and Flash Diffusers for Canon 650D,600D,550D,70D,60D,5D Nikon D5000,D3000,D5100,D3100,D7000,D7100,D800,D800E,D60 While this macro light has some middling quality issues at times, it does offer a viable, and very cost effective alternative to pricier setups.

The light comes with eight lens adapters to cover most of the common applications (49mm, 52mm, 55mm, 58mm, 62mm, 67mm, 72mm, 77mm). The adapters are plastic rather than metal which gives me some concerns about durability. I would have liked to see metal adapters since other low-price setups offer them instead of plastic.

The flash offers a continuous light setting, or a flash setting to time with your exposure. You can set it to use all 48 LEDs or just half (can select either the right or the left half).

It’s powered by a battery pack that takes 4AA batteries. The battery contacts on mine were initially out of place and would not make proper contact with the batteries. After adjusting the position of the contacts with a screwdriver, things worked fine. The screen includes a battery level indicator so you always know how much juice is left.

You can mount the control head on your camera using the hotshoe, or use it off-camera with an included stand. The stand is really light-duty but reasonably functional.

The control head screen is very easy to read. The controls allow for light output brightness adjustments with a simple plus/minus key system, and mode selection (all/half, flash, stead light). There's also a button to test the light output. The buttons are large and well-labeled as to function.

Note that this unit does not allow for delayed/second curtain synch flash.

It includes four diffusers (white, blue, yellow, clear/semi-translucent) that are easy to attach and remove (twist and lift).

I tested this with a Canon 5D mark II and the Canon L 100mm macro and had zero problems with functionality (other than the battery issue listed above).

This is not pro-quality gear but it’s also not pro-level in terms of price. It’s a great way to play around with macro lighting to see if it’s something you find helpful. The all-plastic design keeps this at the 4 star level, but I would certainly recommend it provided you don’t subject it to a lot of heavy use.
[Sample provided for review]

So you spray the spray stuff on, slide the shield around until it's where you want it, then squeegee it down and let it sit. For me, the iPad was completely useable immediately.

What's even better is, a few months later, the corners were lifting and getting some grit under them (not a flaw in the shield ... I was using this with an iPad cover whose silicone covers move a little and shove the shield up). I pulled the corners up, sprayed the solution on (they send way more than you need for one application), flicked off the grit, squeegeed it back down ... good as new!

Given the flexible nature of the film I think a lot of devices that get a lot of rubbing at the edges might get this peeling effect, but it's great how keeping that bottle of spray around lets you fix it right up. When I peeled the corner back i accidentally touched some tissue to the guard, and it stuck to it, and I thought I was done for ... but spraying the liquid solution on, the tissue let go and like I said, it went back down at the corners as good as new.

I'll absolutely be buying these for all future big electronic purchases.

Ring Video Doorbell (1st Gen) – 720p HD video, motion activated alerts, easy installation – Satin Nickel I'm an early adopter of lots of "smart everything" internet connected products (Nest stuff, Smart Grill, SmartVents, internet connected cars, etc.). I have found the Ring doorbell to be one of the most useful and reliable of these types of products. Remote functions that are really valuable to me:
* Remotely "greet" and reschedule the delivery guy who was 2 hours late, while you are out doing other other errands. Warning - it does really freak out most delivery guys to hear your voice emanating from the doorbell button !
* Receive confirmation that your tween/teen has made it home from school, even when they don't see fit to call or text. Plus do a body count to see if any "extras" are visiting. Plus also have a concrete, time-stamped log of any late night returns, so you don't have to stay up late to intercept returning teens.
* Capture video evidence of stolen packages, unwanted solicitations, and prowlers.
The cloud recording cost of 30$/yr is a far better value than other services like Next or Flir. Ring is the clear choice for door monitoring as well as a really cool doorbell.

My only caveats for buyers:
* Take care with the physical installation on very rough surfaces like rough stucco. Holes need to exactly align (no slotted mounting holes) plus the mount plate is sensitive to bending. If the most bends too much to conform to the wall, the actual button/bell unit will not attach.
* Make sure your WiFi signal is strong enough in the location where you are planning install the ring. Plaster and stucco (with embedded screening) attenuate WiFi signals. WiFi basestation with beam-forming really do help (one of my neighbors needed to swap an Apple Airport Express for an Airport Extreme Basestation to achieve reliable and no-laggy video, but now the Ring works like a charm)
* Make sure your transformer is putting out an in-spec voltage, for a wired installation. Mine worked fine, but the another neighbor who recommended the Ring to me wen through two units (replaced by Ring), before they determined the doorbell voltage from the transformer was too high. Things worked flawlessly with the third unit when my neighbor moved to unwired operation.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell (1st Gen) – 720p HD video, motion activated alerts, easy installation – Satin Nickel

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Cloud Cam Security Camera, Works with Alexa What has happened to us???

Why would we --pay money-- for Big Brothe- I mean Amazon- to see into our homes 24/7? After all the smart appliance eavesdropping/conspiracy fiascos last year, and all the privacy rights and issues going on? The 'internet of things' is absolutely hackable. Do you want your home life to be observed and hacked (or deliberately watched!) any more than you want your SSN and credit card numbers being spraypainted in big, clear writing, on the side of a City Bus?

Why would YOU personally, yes you, reading these words, right now, why would YOU want cameras in your home watching you all the time?

What is it you believe about the rest of humanity that makes eternally viewing your possessions or monitoring people in your home, or being in your own home, worth PAYING for?

Seeing something doesn't make you more secure. It might help a lawyer prosecute a criminal. But it won't fix the problems that lead to crime. And it won't prevent a bad thing from happenning. It'll just provide you with a tool to witness it. In detail. Repeatedly. Remember when we all watched those towers go down, over and over for weeks, every day? Yeah. Like that. But YOUR home. Or kids. Or whatever you value enough to feel scared of losing and then feel soothed about that fear by pointing a camera at it.

Knowing your kids are home safe? Can a phone call not verify that? If they are doing somwthing you feel the need to surreptitiously watch, what does that say about your/their abilities to form healthy trust and boundaires and respect in your relationships? And if you catch them doing wrong, could you somehow prevent it from a screen? Like, what's the result of having that evidence of wrongdoing in hand? Is it actually going to be a positive to evoke the changes you seek underneath it all? Is there somethig else that could work better?

Because pointing a security camera just says "I don't trust 'x'." It's not like a baby monitor, and you're in the next room and can respond right away if the need arises. There is a LOT of far LESS INAVSIVE technologies that can accomplish most goals this system is being pitched to solve.

Do you really want to watch whatever events unfold that you might falsely feel you are 'protecting' whatever you think will be protected from, by being able to observe it from afar?

These are PRODUCTS. Designed to make profit for manufacturers. Full stop. How do they sell security? By giving the fear of insecurity to us, and then providing a 'solution.' And at such a great price! Because it's 'introduced'. They literally have introduced us to a fear you maybe we didn't even know we had.

Sure, some of us have been victims of domestic crimes, or have pets or parents or offspring to care for. But products like this only give the illusion that we're actually DOING those things.

It's a way to avoid actual doing.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Cloud Cam Security Camera, Works with Alexa

text_fidelity_a:
Motorola SURFboard SB6121 Cable Modem (SB6121) I read through Comcast supported model list and ordered this from another website, so I didn't have to pay their modem rental fee. I ordered Comcast using the online application process (borrowing a wireless connection from a neighbor), and was forced to order their starter package. Supposedly there is a way to refuse this if you call, but I didn't do this. I had a coax cable with me so as soon as I made my order I connected the modem to the coax input in the apartment, and my wireless router to the modem. I did not use a splitter. With my computer I tried to connect to the web which brought me to the comcast activation screen. I had no issues activating based on the info I had from the box and my comcast account number. This part was easy. It's a good thing I had my own cable since the starter package took two weeks to arrive.

My impression of this modem is that there is nothing special to this modem.You can access the modem through its IP address, which gives you several tabs: Status, Signal, Addresses Configuration, Logs, Open Source. No password is needed. You can remotely reboot it, and check to see if there is a signal. Other than that one feature I wished it had is having the ability to export logs. When the modem reboots, the logs get reset.

I have used a DOCSIS 2.0 modem at another location and I think the level of service makes a bigger difference than the DOCSIS version of the modem in use. You might see a difference if you pay for the top end ISP package, but I didn't get that. My plan is Performance which is supposed to be 50 Mbps, but my actual speed is 29 up 6 down.

I have read of some cases of the modem randomly rebooting. I don't have this issue. But I did open my modem and attached an aluminum heat sink as a precaution. I have managed to fit 100x25x10mm heatsink by cutting off a section. From what I read random reboots might be ISP related, but I'm not sure.

*****

As a side note, Comcast is terrible. At one point my service suddenly stopped. One tech service person I talked to hung up on me after half an hour of troubleshooting when see seemingly ran out of ideas to try. The next time I called I demanded a technician, which was scheduled to show up in 10 days at the earliest. I had a service outage for almost a month. The issue was a loose cable in their box. Also at one point my Netflix streaming was heavily throttled until Netlix payed off Comcast.
text_fidelity_b: Motorola SURFboard SB6121 Cable Modem (SB6121)

I have downgraded the Amazfit Bip Smartwatch from 5-Stars to 1-Star. This is why:

Sorry to say, my opinion is the Bip does NOT WORK WITH ANDROID 8.1. That seemingly the case, what will happen when Android P, now in Beta, releases as Android 9 in August, 2018?

I'm going back to my iPhone/Apple Watch. Yes, that combination has glitches as well. However, support for Apple Products is always reliable and you're not stuck texting for help.
