text_fidelity_a:
Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Full-Sized 2.4GHz Wireless Keyboard with Comfortable Palm Rest and Optical Wireless Mouse for Windows, Mac OS PC/Desktops/Computer/Laptops I've used much worse keyboards and mice, but I've also used much better. The keyboard is not bad, but speed typists would definitely prefer better. Because this is a full-size keyboard, be aware that you'll need ample space on your pull-out keyboard drawer. Some office desks have very narrow and shallow drawers. The mouse is okay too but feels a little cheap. However, this product was obviously not intended to be top-end.

My main criticism of this package is the somewhat confusing owner's manual. Every USB product I've used, particularly a kb or mouse, are plug-and-play. The manual gave instructions for "repairing' with the device, and it was unclear why you would need to issue the series of key commands in order to reconnect via USB on a PC. Perhaps this connection procedure applies only to other types of devices. After one brief failed attempt to connect (see next paragraph), the second try connected okay after I plugged in the USB dongle. I also unplugged/replugged the dongle and it worked again, without having to issue any of the "Esc + K" keypresses that the manual stated were necessary to repair the devices.

I suspect the range of this pairing is not very far. The first time I plugged the dongle in, neither the kb nor the mouse worked. I had to move both closer to the dongle before I got them to connect. The kb and mouse were only four feet from the dongle when I first installed them. After I finally got everything to connect at close range, I moved the kb and mouse back to the distance of four feet, and they continued to work. So I'm not sure of what distance would cause a disconnect.
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Full-Sized 2.4GHz Wireless Keyboard with Comfortable Palm Rest and Optical Wireless Mouse for Windows, Mac OS PC/Desktops/Computer/Laptops

text_fidelity_a:
Clip-Case Universal Ergonomic Tablet Stand (Tripod Kit) and Smartphone Mount for iPhone iPad iPod Galaxy Droid Kindle Nook This is one of those "why didn't I think of it?" type products. At first glance, it seems quite simple - basically a mini tripod with attachments that allow you to mount a tablet or phone. But after working with it for a while, it's clear a lot of thought went into this.

The tripod is well made and sturdy, consisting mainly of metal. The ball joint at the top is controlled by a built-in key that allows you to loosen and tighten it so it stays put. Each leg extends independently, so you can set the tripod so it is tilted upward (for example, to position a tablet so you can watch a movie at your desk). The attachment screw base has a rubber non-slip insert to protect whatever you're attaching against scratches. It includes a lanyard, but you can easily remove it (which I did) if it's not needed.

The tripod is very compact -- folds up to about 4.5 inches long and about 1 inch wide, so it's easy to carry. With the legs fully extended it is just under 9 inches tall. The legs have a thick rubber tip that keep it well balanced and positioned. I was a bit concerned that the legs didn't have locks, but the tension of the pull out extensions was more than adequate to keep the legs extended even when it was loaded down with an 8.9 inch Kindle Fire.

Impressive quality given the price - much better than expected.

You can also use the tripod as a camera tripod since the attachment screw is a standard size. It worked fine with my Panasonic and Canon point and shoots.

But the star of the show is the clip. You attach it to the back of the device case (you could attach it to the device itself, but it's not recommended) using an adhesive pad. The pad is removable, but is not reusable, so you want to give some thought before you stick it to the case. Once attached, it fits into a "smart mount" that, in turn, attaches to the tripod. Sounds kind of complicated, but it's very simple to use. There is an included instruction sheet, but you can pretty much puzzle it out by just looking at it.

The clip and smart mount are plastic, but seem more than sturdy enough for the job. They clip together with an interlocking system that kept my Kindle very solidly positioned while I was using it.

The only negative I see is the adhesive pad. As with any adhesive, you need to clean the point of contact very well (an alcohol pad is included in the box) and let the adhesive cure for 30 min. I think it's a safe bet that some people won't do both those steps, which opens the door to a significant point of failure.

But, provided you read the instructions, this is a very nicely designed and useful product. Highly recommend.
[The manufacturer provided the product for review]
text_fidelity_b: Clip-Case Universal Ergonomic Tablet Stand (Tripod Kit) and Smartphone Mount for iPhone iPad iPod Galaxy Droid Kindle Nook

text_fidelity_a:
iHome iAVS16 Bedside Speaker with Alexa Built In, Bluetooth, and USB Charging, Now Supports Spotify by Voice There are both positives and negatives about this product, my perspective being that I am using it to replace an old-sko0l red LED alarm buzzer with staticy radio.

+ Looks sleeker (one would hope, as the old had a plastic wood finish), smaller footprint, and slightly raised clock makes it easier to see.

+ I love the USB port, so I can get rid of two power cords and replace it with one.

+ Shows the weather as according to Accuweather, which is at least a rough estimate of what it's like outside.

+ Better sound if you want to set it to stream music.

+ Shows the date.

+ 2 programmable buttons allow you to control "smart" devices. This could be really handy if you have a light for the room plugged into a receptacle across the room. You could also cut your overhead light cord and put in a socket for control from your bed if you're into that sort of thing. I just have a lamp beside the bed, so I really don't care, but this is something I can actually see being useful.

+ Can use it as a Bluetooth speaker. Would be better if you could integrate it with other home WiFi speakers, even though I'm more into big, hardwired speakers for serious listening from a whole-house audio system

Things that are both positive and negative, so I guess I have to call them neutral:

= microphone has a button to turn it off. A switch would be more believable, and then it wouldn't have a red light showing on the top all the time. I have no doubts the CIA can still turn it on, but I like to think the manufacturer won't listen in. I'm sure they could have put a back door in, too, but I would hope they would be sued severely if that is ever discovered. The red light is good when talking on the phone to show the phone is muted but otherwise the light shouldn't be on all the time...

= Buttons on the top are always lit up, which I consider to be a negative. Should be able to control them separately. Front display has 6 dim levels and off, and the lowest level is good for sleeping even with the thing pointed at you (at least in my opinion), but then it's really not bright enough during the day (at least if it's a bright day). I know it's petty, but I'm really not into doing anything more than I already do to get ready for bed, and that includes pressing a button 5 or 6 times to get it back to the way I wanted it. Should work on a light sensor or just be able to program it for day and evening. I mention this stuff because I'm sure it can be added via firmware (not the sensor part, obviously). Overall, not as bright as the old red LED thing, but somehow less see-able.

= You can do random light shows with the colored LEDs at the bottom. I suppose setting it to come on before your alarm is useful, but just playing with them is not.

Negatives:

- I just hate the Internet sometimes, and this reminds me why. (I'm a fairly young Systems Engineer, FYI, so it's not that I'm some geezer that can't use technology). I just hate that I need an app to control this thing. It's an alarm clock, so shouldn't I be able to do the basics without my phone? Is this just so they can get on my phone and steal my data/identity/whatever? I got news for you guys - I set this kind of crap up with a burner phone that is linked to fake Email, fake everything, location and everything else turned off. Let me at least set the bloody time without hooking up to the Internet! What happens when Comcast freezes and my WiFi temporarily doesn't have Internet connection?

To use Spotify with this (which I don't use and never will since I just have all the music I could ever want on a local server), you have to buy the Premium version. I'm sure that was absolutely necessary. Is anything not contrived multi-layered big business anymore?

Just to DL the app, Google and my burner phone both try to trick me into thinking I have to put credit card details in to get it. Sometimes I'm just ready to forego the digital age and find an old ticking clock that loses 5 minutes every day to run my life by. I am so sick and tired of adds, apps that want to control and steal your life, and companies that can't think further than next quarter...

- No battery backup. Should be built in. Even my '70s POS could be backed up via 9v battery. It saves some settings, but turns back to archaic Fahrenheit on me when power is lost...

- ...worse...when power comes back on, it screams at you. Power in my area is good, but on occasion goes out for a few seconds multiple times in a night. That may be the end of this thing (OK, I just lowered my star rating to 3, because the truth is, that probably will be the end of this thing's reign in my bedroom).

- No radio. No internal memory for music. You're at the mercy of streaming accounts and everything working properly on your network.

- Going along with the first negative point, you can't even set an alarm with this thing if you don't sign in with an Amazon account and do the Alexa thing. More ways to get grips on you. More ways to complicate a simple alarm clock.

Do I really hate simple and easy so much? I almost gave this four stars due to the fact that it looks pretty and adds some functionality, but what's wrong with a highly visible dump clock beside the bed? That's all I'm using this for, when it all comes down to it. Well, my feelings may change for the better when they inevitably fix some of the simple things on this that they can do by firmware. I will let you know if my feelings change significantly.
text_fidelity_b: iHome iAVS16 Bedside Speaker with Alexa Built In, Bluetooth, and USB Charging, Now Supports Spotify by Voice

The unit itself is solid, and offers the ability to hold 6 CDs (and shuffle play). The changer works well -- no glitches so far after a few weeks of heavy use. Nice styling with an easy to see display. The buttons on the unit are a bit hard to see, but you'll quickly figure out what controls what.

I'm using this with an Onkyo receiver, so it can take advantage of the Onkyo interface (i.e., power up the CD player and the receiver automatically powers up as well and changes the input to CD). Only two cables to connect -- an optical out and the Onkyo interface cable.

The size is somewhat imposing (both height and depth). As other reviewers have mentioned, check the size specs before you buy to make sure it fits into the cabinet/rack you want to use.

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS ZenPad 3S 10 9.7" (2048x1536), 4GB RAM, 64GB eMMC, 5MP Front / 8MP Rear Camera, Android 6.0, Tablet, Glacier Silver (Z500M-C1-SL) As a long-time Apple user, I am strongly considering other options because of a number of issues, including software updates that slow to a halt older devices ("planned obsolescence" is what they call it). Between that, the higher cost, and a few other things, I'm in the market for a different tablet and computer.

In the past, the problem switching back was that, unlike with Apple, things were not quite as user friendly with the interface and you had to really figure things out instead of it being immediately apparent.

Happily, it was different with this tablet. Out of the box, my family and I were able to figure it out quickly and easily, giving us hope in another option.

Quality: Great image on the screen with very high resolution! The feel of the device is also sturdy, aesthetically pleasing, lightweight, and thin.

User-friendly layout, very accessible, good features, and it works seamlessly with Google. I've got google email and YouTube channels, so it's nice to know there's a trade-off for losing some of the other things like seamless transitions between iTunes, my current calendar (not in love with that--I can just as easily switch to google or droid for this)...

All this adds up to the following: Apple can no longer claim to be the clear leader in tablets, phones, and computers. They have stopped innovating far beyond comparable products, and now, for the value and overall performance, the ZenPad is a worthy adversary.

I still have my MacBook Pro computer, but when it comes time to buy a new one, I will be ready to switch knowing items like these are available.
What a great surprise!
text_fidelity_b: ASUS ZenPad 3S 10 9.7" (2048x1536), 4GB RAM, 64GB eMMC, 5MP Front / 8MP Rear Camera, Android 6.0, Tablet, Glacier Silver (Z500M-C1-SL)

text_fidelity_a: SanDisk 256GB Ultra Dual Drive USB Type-C - USB-C, USB 3.1 - SDDDC2-256G-G46 I use this to transfer files in a multi-platform (Macs & PCs) environment. Having both the standard USB interface and the newer USB-C interface in the same thumb drive is very handy. The device is fairly compact considering the two connectors are both recessed for travel. It gets a bit warm during heavy transfer activity, but not enough to be a problem. The only reason I didn’t give 5 stars is because it is fairly slow for large files. And, by large files we’re talking anything over 2GBs, so not that large. Moving 10-15 GBs takes several minutes. I also have an older version of this device and it was just as slow. Therefore, I’d say even though they have upgraded the product standard to USB 3.1, it appears to be the same chip as the older version and the chip is the limiting factor. If you need a multi-platform capable thumb drive, this is a worthwhile purchase. But don’t expect fast transfer speeds.

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic Bluetooth Earbud Headphones with Microphone, Call/Volume Controller and Quick Charge Function - RP-HJE120B-R - in-Ear Headphones (Red) These wireless, Bluetooth earbuds are a terrific invention. They totally eliminate the bane of earbud existence--tangling wires. The sound quality, however, is only about as good as the inexpensive earbuds I usually buy. The justification for these earbuds being four times as expensive as low-cost earbuds is spelled out in one word: convenience. Bluetooth wireless technology is convenient because it eliminates wires.

These earbuds paired easily with my iPhone 5c, and the remote controller, which is contained in the right earpiece, is user friendly and works well. You can control the volume that way or via your smart phone.

These earbuds offer three sizes of ear cushions, small, medium and large.

As is true for any Bluetooth device, these ear buds must be charged. Like my Bluetooth, this device uses a Micro-USB port which is within the controller. It takes about 4 hours to charge fully after fully drained, and the charge lasts about 90 minutes. A partial charge takes 20 minutes and lasts 60 minutes, or so the maker claims. The math doesn't add up for those two claims. So far I've been charging it several hours at a time, and switching off between other earbuds while it is charging. It's a bit frustrating that this device doesn't hold a charge very long. And I find that rather surprising since my iPhone's Bluetooth holds a charge for up to 11 hours.

These earbuds are very comfortable in the ears, but I don't like wearing them as the product information pictures them, with the hanging cords behind the neck. I find it far more comfortable and balanced when worn in the front.

These earbuds have three buttons on a controller which is located by the right ear piece. They consist of: on/off, play/pause/answer, Bluetooth pairing button, volumn control, next track button, rewind track button. They work as advertised.

A microphone is included within the controller. This means if you are listening to music or other entertainment media on your iPhone, if you get a call, you can use this device like a regular Bluetooth and take the call. I have used this device for calls, and I can hear fine, and so can the person on the other end of the call.

I had no problem pairing the device with my iPhone. The distance of reach is supposed to be up to 30 feet, but it's not that far inside a building because of the dividing walls from room to room. It's more like 15-20 feet.

Negatives include the fact that the warranty is a measly 90 days, the cost is a high price to pay mainly for convenience, it doesn't hold a charge very long, and it is made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic Bluetooth Earbud Headphones with Microphone, Call/Volume Controller and Quick Charge Function - RP-HJE120B-R - in-Ear Headphones (Red)

text_fidelity_a:
Coby Kyros 7-Inch Android 2.3 4 GB Internet Touchscreen Tablet - MID7012-4G (Black) I never owned a tablet or a smartphone so I suppose if I did my review might be different but I think this is a pretty neat little tablet and the price is pretty great too.

I've had it for a couple of days and downloaded the Amazon App store which has most of the apps anyone could need. I mean seriously how many apps does an average person really use? I have downloaded quite a few games for both myself and my kids, the Kindle app, I heart Radio app, and the US newspaper app. So far its holding all of it but I also ordered a microsdhc card for extra space to hold more apps and e-books. I have a regular Kindle that I've had for quite a few years and I am able to transfer most of the books onto this tablet also (I haven't tried downloading all of them since my son uses a few for school). It has where you can calibrate the stylus. Also if you longpress the stylus onto the wallpaper it will let you change the wallpaper in the background.

It does not come with a camera and flashplayer is not installed (but what I understand you can install a "lite" version of flashplayer which I have not done as of yet). The touchscreen is more geared toward using the stylus (which is included) which is a let down to some people. You can use your fingertip but it isn't as responsive as with the stylus IMO. It also comes with a sleeve (that has a place for your stylus) and earphones. There is a charger and a USB cable. There is another cable which I'm not sure exactly what its for (sorry). I haven't used the other cables just yet (except the charger of course). As for battery life it does seem like it runs down pretty quickly (perhaps 3-4 hours). Of course, that may change depending on the type of apps you have running. I know a lot of people worry about reading books from this rather than the Kindle type e-ink. I, personally, like reading at night before I go to sleep and with the Kindle I had to keep a lamp on just to see the page..(barely)...whereas this isn't like that (my eyes are much happier!) You can change the brightness of the screen if you are worried about the brightness bothering your eyes.

I have my email accessible to the Coby Kyros so I can check it throughout the day since my daughter takes off with my laptop quite often. I also downloaded the Dolphin mini browser which I like better than the browser sent with the Kyros. It comes with the GetJar app store which has quite a few apps but Amazon has more.

Of course, I cannot guarantee how well it will hold up because I've only had it for a couple of days but overall its a nice simple little tablet. I've seen the reviews of more expensive tablets and I don't want to spend $400 on a tablet that's rated two stars. I was willing to take the chance and so far I'm happy with my purchase. I rated it 4 stars because the speaker is kinda crappy...I haven't tried listening to the radio with earphones...hopefully it sounds better. And also I wish that it was easier to install flash (I've been looking on the internet but it seems like you have to be really a techie to do it...and I'm not!) It's not an Ipad (or Ipod) so you can't rate this tablet against a product like that (of course it's half the price of a Ipod touch).
text_fidelity_b: Coby Kyros 7-Inch Android 2.3 4 GB Internet Touchscreen Tablet - MID7012-4G (Black)
